issues.legal_issue: Payments received for ending or surrendering business interests under compromise or amicable arrangement are taxable as income when they are profits received for the interest held in the business.
material_facts: The assessee had obtained interests in a sugar mill through a transfer and leases from other partners.

After one partner challenged a lease, the parties compromised, terminated the lease and arranged payments to the assessee; another partner returned the leased share under a mutual arrangement and also agreed to make payments.
The assessee treated the payments as capital receipts in lieu of the leasehold interests.
issues.conclusion: The payments were profits received for the assessee’s interests in the business and were taxable income.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the receipts under the compromise and amicable arrangement as profits for interests held in the business, rather than as capital receipts. The Court relied on no identified statutory provision or named earlier case for this conclusion.

predicates.business_income_assessment: The proceeding determines the income-tax treatment of a receipt.
predicates.compromise_payment_for_business_interest: A person receives a payment under a compromise for ending or changing an interest held in a business.
predicates.amicable_payment_for_business_interest: A person receives a payment by amicable arrangement for ending or changing an interest held in a business.

issues.definition: When an income-tax assessment concerns a payment received by compromise or amicable arrangement for ending or changing a business interest, the payment is treated as taxable income.

issues.legal_issue: Depreciation is not allowable to a claimant who establishes only a fractional share in property rather than ownership of the property.
material_facts: The assessee claimed depreciation on machinery in a sugar mill based on a one-sixth share acquired from another partner.
The assessee did not claim to be the full owner of the machinery.
issues.conclusion: The depreciation claim based on the fractional share was not allowable.
issues.legal_principle: Section 10(2)(vi) of the Income-tax Act, 1922 permits depreciation in respect of buildings, machinery, plant or furniture that is the property of the assessee. The Court held that the assessee must be the owner and that a fractional claim does not suffice. No identified earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

predicates.depreciation_claim: A claimant seeks a depreciation allowance for property.
predicates.fractional_property_ownership: The claimant establishes only a fractional share in the property, rather than ownership of the property as a whole.

issues.definition: A depreciation claim based only on a fractional share in property is denied.

issues.legal_issue: A carried-forward business loss may be set off only against business income from the same business in which the loss was incurred.
material_facts: The assessee had an unabsorbed loss from its sugar business.
It sought to set off that loss against its share of rent received from the Receiver for the sugar mill.
The Receiver had been appointed in connection with dissolution of the firm, and the factory was operated principally to enable its sale as a running mill for a proper price.
Letting out the mill was not the assessee’s business.
issues.conclusion: The carried-forward loss could not be set off against the rent because letting out the mill was not the same business in which the loss had been incurred.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24 of the Income-tax Act, 1922 required both that the income against which the loss was set off be business income and that the income be from the same business in which the loss was suffered. The Court referred to prior decisions, including a decision of this Court reported at 26 ITR 765, without identifying its title.

predicates.carried_forward_business_loss_setoff_cla: A taxpayer seeks to set off an unabsorbed loss from a business against later income.
predicates.income_is_not_business_income: The income against which the taxpayer seeks to set off the loss is not income from a business.
predicates.income_is_not_from_loss_business: The income against which the taxpayer seeks to set off the loss is not from the business in which the loss was incurred.

issues.definition: A carried-forward business loss is not set off when the income against which it is claimed is not business income or is not from the business that incurred the loss.

issues.legal_issue: A Receiver cannot obtain a separate depreciation basis for a portion of business assets when the business is assessed as an association of persons and the depreciation claim is maintained for the assessed entity.
material_facts: The sugar mill was in a Receiver’s hands and was assessed as an association of persons.
A partner had acquired another partner’s one-sixth share in the mill under an exchange valued at a stated amount.
The Receiver sought to increase the written-down value of the business assets to reflect that stated value for the acquired share.
The claim was rejected by the tax authorities and the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The Receiver’s claim to increase the written-down value by separately valuing the acquired share was rejected; the book value applied to the entire assets of the firm.
issues.legal_principle: Under the scheme of the Income-tax Act, 1922, only the assessee is entitled to maintain a depreciation claim, and a separate value for a part of the assets could not be maintained for calculating depreciation. The Court applied section 10(2)(vi) in the context of the statutory depreciation scheme and relied on its conclusion that a fractional share did not qualify for depreciation. No additional named earlier case was cited for this issue.

predicates.depreciation_claim: A claim is made to calculate a depreciation allowance for business assets.
predicates.business_assessed_as_association: The business is assessed for tax as an association of persons.
predicates.receiver_seeks_separate_asset_valuation: A Receiver seeks to assign a separate value to part of the business assets to calculate depreciation.

issues.definition: When a business assessed as an association has a depreciation claim, a Receiver’s request to separately value part of its assets for that calculation is denied.
